implementation_notes: The synchronized block is a language feature that implements the pattern directly: the JVM emits monitorenter/monitorexit with an implicit exception handler, so the monitor is released on normal completion and on abrupt completion. POSA2 lists the Java synchronized block as a language implementation of Scoped Locking. Monitors are reentrant, so intra-object calls re-acquire instead of self-deadlocking (they just add hold counts). Synchronizing a method is the same mechanism with the whole method as the scope.
pitfalls: Locking on `this` or on a Class object exposes the monitor to outside code - prefer a dedicated private final lock object.
The intrinsic monitor offers no timeout, no try-acquire and no interruptible acquire; use ReentrantLock when cancellation or bounded waiting is required.
Virtual threads pin their carrier thread inside synchronized blocks, so blocking there destroys the scalability benefit; reentrant locks avoid pinning.
Holding the monitor while calling foreign code (listeners, callbacks) is a classic deadlock and long-hold-time source.

variants.name: ReentrantLock with try/finally (Java 5)
variants.implementation_notes: java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock provides the same mutual exclusion with explicit release: lock() to acquire, unlock() in a finally so the scope-bound guarantee holds, plus fairness, tryLock with timeout, lockInterruptibly and multiple Condition queues. Choose it when the intrinsic monitor's limits matter - interruptible or bounded acquisition, condition objects, or lock hand-over between threads - and accept that, unlike C#'s lock statement, nothing in the compiler enforces the finally.
pitfalls: Forgetting the finally defeats the pattern; there is no compile-time check.
unlock() in a finally can throw IllegalMonitorStateException if the lock was never acquired (for example an interrupted lockInterruptibly) and mask the original exception.
Reentrancy hides design problems and hold counts must be balanced; prefer tryLock with a timeout at component boundaries.
A Condition must be awaited in a loop that re-checks the predicate, and only while holding the lock.
